A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SKADA-Bench study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and alignable despite pagination and presentation changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original domain-adaptation benchmark experiments, including accuracy results, scorer comparisons, and supplementary analyses in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark results and adds a Spearman correlation analysis of validation scores and target accuracy.

M1.justification: The benchmark pipeline, adaptation procedures, and neural architectures remain unchanged. Section 3.2 expands descriptions of DAN, MDD, MCC, and SPA, which were already evaluated in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate four simulated shift types and the same eight real-world datasets covering 51 adaptation tasks. Larger datasets discussed in v4 are proposed future work.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding main and appendix tables. Tables 3 and 21 already contain seven deep methods in v2; changing the introductory count from three to seven does not add evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds Spearman correlation as a supplemental scorer-evaluation metric in Figure 6, retaining the Pearson analysis in Figure 3. Data splits, preprocessing, training budgets, architectures, and hyperparameter grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.6 adds a rank-correlation cross-check of whether validation scores track target accuracy, supporting the existing scorer analysis. Base-estimator comparisons, F1 analysis, scorer-ranking analyses, and computational-efficiency experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 6 adds Spearman rank-correlation estimates alongside the existing Pearson estimates. This is a limited addition to statistical analysis; split counts, standard-deviation reporting, and Wilcoxon significance-testing procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: Benchmark accuracy, F1, and ranking tables are unchanged. New Figure 6 reports Spearman coefficients including CircV 0.63, IW 0.32, and MixVal 0.12. A new under-20-second runtime statement in Section 4.1 conflicts with the unchanged runtime figure, which places LinOT at roughly 35 seconds.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and distribution-shift assumptions in Section 2.1 are unchanged. Formula annotations added to Figure 1 restate existing relationships; no new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the claimed deep-method coverage from three to seven, matching results already present in v2. The central contributions concerning realistic validation, diverse modalities, and shallow-versus-deep comparisons remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds explicit limitations concerning variance from the single outer split and restrictions imposed by the four-hour budget. It recommends larger datasets and more stable evaluation for future work, qualifying previously reported deep-method findings.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A replace deferred-release statements with present code-availability statements, although v2 already provided the repository URL in its abstract. v4 also names the Inria and IP Paris computing infrastructures. Implementation examples and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference lists and substantive positioning relative to earlier DA research are unchanged. Expanded descriptions of deep methods reuse works already cited and evaluated in v2.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized prose revisions, expands preprocessing explanations, adds numerical examples and short computational-cost and limitations passages, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised colors and mathematical annotations, and a new Spearman plot becomes Figure 6. Existing appendix plots are retained and renumbered. Journal headers, first-page composition, and figure placement change without a broad redesign of the tables.

improvement.justification: The Spearman cross-check adds useful support for scorer conclusions, while explicit limitations better qualify the single-split deep-method results. Clearer code-access statements also improve transparency. These modest gains outweigh a localized new reporting error: the under-20-second runtime summary conflicts with LinOT's roughly 35 seconds in Figure 11. The underlying experimental precision is unchanged.
